key_concepts: Plant reproduction can be sexual or asexual
Sexual reproduction fuses gametes and produces genetically different offspring
Asexual reproduction produces genetically identical offspring without gamete fusion
Flower reproductive parts include receptacle, petal, sepal, pistil, and stamen
Stamen is the male part with anther and filament
Pistil is the female part with stigma, style, and ovary
Petals attract insects; sepals protect the flower bud
Pollination transfers pollen from anther to stigma
Fertilization fuses sperm and egg inside an ovule
After fertilization the ovule becomes a seed and an embryo forms
Germination is seed growth requiring soil, water, and sunlight
Vegetative reproduction uses rhizomes, stolons, bulbs, tubers, and corms
